annotations.text:
Login — chosen: D1's login, then the step-by-step 'check your email' from D3 without its progress strip. Expired link unchanged.
First time, a new person never sees these: the invite email and one click log them in. These screens are for later — new phone, or logged out.

The flow
1 · type your email, get a link
2 · open the email and tap the button — you land on your own main screen (technician: today's log, engineer: the dashboard)
3 · only if the link is over 24 hours old or already used: ask for a new one

Invite — chosen: the team list with the add form beside it (P2). Phone: the same list, with the form as a bottom sheet.
Shown: an Engineer adding a Technician. The Owner adds an Engineer the same way. The role comes from who is adding; the project is picked in the form.
On send, the new person gets the email below and is in with one click.

The team list shows each person's status — Aktiv / Në pritje / Çaktivizuar — with resend and deactivate on each row (on phone: tap the person). The add form slides in beside the list, so you can see who's already on the team while adding.

The invite email — the real first impression
Says who invited you, to which project, in what role; one big button; the 24-hour limit and what to do if it runs out.
Sending it for real needs a proper email service (Supabase's built-in sender is for testing only).

Not chosen — kept for the record.
Rows 1–3: the first round of login ideas (A/B/C), replaced by the invite-link decision.
Row 4: second-round login screens that weren't picked.
Row 5: the full-page invite form (P1) — the team list with a side panel was picked instead.

A — Email + password
Why: the familiar one. Supabase has it built in, no extra cost. With "keep me signed in", the engineer logs in once on his phone and stays logged in.
Tradeoff: typing a password on a phone on site, maybe with gloves on — and passwords get forgotten.

B — Phone number + SMS code
Why: no password to remember or type — suits the engineer on site, and everyone already has a phone.
Tradeoff: needs an SMS provider (e.g. Twilio) connected to Supabase — a cost per SMS, plus setup. The PM on desktop needs his phone at hand to log in.

C — Tap your name + 4-digit PIN
Why: the fastest — one tap and four digits, with a big keypad that works with gloves. Logs in by itself after the 4th digit.
Tradeoff: the weakest security — fine for a pilot with a few people, not for many users. Supabase doesn't offer it built in, so it has to be built ourselves.

Round 2, not picked
D1's 'check your email' — replaced by the step-by-step one.
D2 'Site (bold)' — both states: built for sun and gloves, but loud next to the rest of the app.
D3's login — D1's was preferred.
D3's original 'check your email' — the chosen screen is this one without the progress strip.

P1 — Full-page invite form, not picked
Simplest to build, but you leave the team list while adding and can't see who's already on the team. The list + side panel was picked instead.
